title: Smoothness over a product ring is checked factorwise
statement: Let $\varphi_1:R_1\to A_1$ and $\varphi_2:R_2\to A_2$ be homomorphisms of commutative rings, and make $A_1\times A_2$ an $R_1\times R_2$-algebra via $\varphi_1\times\varphi_2:(r_1,r_2)\mapsto(\varphi_1(r_1),\varphi_2(r_2))$. If $\varphi_1$ and $\varphi_2$ are smooth ring maps [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map], then $\varphi_1\times\varphi_2:R_1\times R_2\to A_1\times A_2$ is a smooth ring map.

source.place: No Stacks lemma states it in this form; Stacks uses it implicitly in Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma Tag 07F3 (smoothing.tex line 1926). It follows from Algebra, Lemma Tag 0GIF (lemma-product-smooth, line 37613: a product S'xS'' of R-algebras is smooth over R iff both factors are) applied over R = R_1 x R_2, together with Lemma Tag 00TD (lemma-compose-smooth, line 37597) for R_1 x R_2 -> R_k -> A_k, where the projection R_1 x R_2 -> R_1 is the principal localization at the idempotent (1,0) (smooth, e.g. standard smooth R[x]/((1,0)x-1), Lemma Tag 00T7 lemma-standard-smooth)

proof.text: Put R = R₁ × R₂ and equip R₁ and R₂ with the algebra structures induced by RingHom.fst and RingHom.snd. Mathlib.RingTheory.Etale.Basic supplies Algebra.Etale R R₁ and Algebra.Etale R R₂ for these exact structures, in independent universes. The étale-to-smooth instance gives smoothness of both projections. These instances use localization away from (1,0) and (0,1), respectively; no polynomial presentation is needed.

source.place: Principal localization at the two idempotents, as in the original source; implemented by the proved product-projection instances in Mathlib.RingTheory.Etale.Basic.

proof.text: Equip A₁ with the R-algebra structure induced by φ₁ composed with fst, and A₂ with that induced by φ₂ composed with snd. Each scalar-tower law holds definitionally, proved by IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq' rfl. Apply Algebra.Smooth.comp [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-base-change-composition] to each smooth projection and the corresponding hypothesis to obtain Smooth R A₁ and Smooth R A₂.

Apply Algebra.Smooth.prod [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-product-algebra] over R. Prod.algebra for the two composite structure maps is definitionally RingHom.toAlgebra (RingHom.prodMap φ₁ φ₂), so its conclusion is exactly the required Smooth structure without any transport or change of statement.

proof_origin.place: Original localization/composition/product argument, using proved Mathlib étale projection instances instead of the standard smooth polynomial presentation; composition by Mathlib Algebra.Smooth.comp, product by the existing Sheaf Algebra.Smooth.prod.

split_report.summary: Definition used: def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map is Stacks 00T2 (finite presentation, H_1(NL)=0, Omega finite projective), so the proof goes only through stated lemmas about smooth maps, not through formal smoothness. Route as in the node's source: (1) the projection R_1 x R_2 -> R_1 has the standard smooth presentation R[x]/((1,0)x-1) with Jacobian (1,0) mapping to 1, kernel computation written out, smooth by lem-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-is-smooth (00T7); (2) R_1 x R_2 -> R_1 -> A_1 smooth by composition (00TD, existing leaf lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-base-change-composition); (3) the product over R_1 x R_2 by the 'if' direction of Stacks 0GIF, new unsplit node lem-weil-pbc-smooth-product-algebra (Mathlib has formal smoothness and finite presentation of finite Pi products, recorded as mathlib_candidate; no Algebra.Smooth for products), and the product structure map equals phi_1 x phi_2. The principal-localization route (lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-principal-localization) would need R -> R smooth for the identity, which the 00T2 definition does not give in one line; the standard smooth presentation avoids it. Citer lem-weil-pbc-popescu-product step 2 uses exactly the statement. Mathlib: no match (searches recorded on the node, one loogle added).
